reviewer: Independent AI reviewer with no builder context. Not a human. The generator (build.py), test_laneway.py, verify.py, candidate.json, README.md, evidence/ and integration/ were not opened, and neither were build-report.json or delivery-verification.json.
scope: Repeat holistic, source-locked Gate G architectural-clay review of the exact v006 GLB for vancouver_laneway_house / laneway_garden_studio (variant 3) against the three locked references. Re-tests every v004 finding, checks each builder-claimed change, and runs a full regression of fidelity, all four sides, the roof weathering graph, openings, supports and contacts, visibility and cameras, from pixels first with GLB measurement as support. The images govern over the catalogue text; per the human ruling the variant is renamed Garage Suite. This review grants no keeper, runtime-activation or publication approval.
decision_note: v006 is a clear improvement. The roof is fixed: a 2.0 m ridge with steeper front and back faces now registers to the fitted top view within about 5 px. The corner box reads as a glazed wrap. The stoop, balcony end, garage lining and mortar are fixed, and the massing still registers in both fitted views. One P1 remains, carried from v004 P1-03. The lane ground window and band slots now have the right widths (0.87 m and 0.50 m), but their glass sits 0.135 m deep in the reveals. At the grazing street and oblique reference angles that hides most of the glass, so in match_front, match_oblique and both phone boards they still read as dark slits where the references show glazed windows. The fix is finite: bring those frames near-flush. Eight P2 notes remain, including one new regression: a hairline on the upper street face where the extended garage lining now reaches the exterior. Gate G needs zero P0 and P1, so this needs a new bounded version, a complete rerender and a repeat independent review.

findings.title: Lane-face ground window and band slots still read as dark slits from both reference cameras: openings are now the right width, but the glass sits 0.135 m deep in the reveals
evidence: GLB: ground lane window opening Y 0.08..0.95 (0.87 m) in the cedar face at X 7.90, but frame X 7.73..7.80 and glass X 7.765, i.e. 0.135 m behind the face. Band slots: opening Y 5.22..5.72 (0.50 m) in the panel face at X 7.95, but frame X 7.78..7.85 and glass X 7.815, also 0.135 m deep. Both widths match the builder's claims.

The street camera sees the lane face at about 15 degrees, so a 0.135 m reveal hides about 0.5 m of glass. Reviewer ray sweep with the builder's match_front camera: ground window 5.0 px of first-hit glass across a 14.3 px opening; each slot 0.0 px across 5.7-6.5 px openings. With match_oblique: ground window about 15 of 29 px; slots about 1 of 12-13 px.

variant_3.png: the ground lane window (about x 743-763, y 442-533) shows about 17 px of glass in a thin frame, as wide as the corner pane above it. Both slots (about x 824-833, y 297-367 and y 457-527) show glazing with reflections.

match_front.png: the ground window reads as a narrow dark sliver (about x 756-763) beside a lit cedar reveal (about x 763-769). The slots (about x 826-832, y 300-370 and 455-525) are dark recesses with no glass. Side-by-side crops: scratch crops/v6_lanewin_zoom.png, crops/v6_slots_front.png.

variant_3_angle_60.jpg against match_oblique.png: the reference ground window (about x 722-748) and slots (upper about x 838-853) read as glazed. In the model the ground window is a slit with a wide lit reveal, and the slots are dark recesses (scratch crops/v6_lane_obl_zoom.png).

phone-street.png: the reference lane face shows a full ground window (about x 768-786, y 625-712) and two glazed slots; the model shows a thin slit (about x 778-790, y 1432-1525) and two dark lines (about x 848-856). phone-oblique.png shows the same contrast (reference about x 643-665, y 712-790; model about x 650-662, y 1520-1590).
Seen square-on, the openings read correctly (right_side.png, band_contact.png, reviewer r_lane_low.png). The defect is in the source-matched read at the reference cameras, not in the opening sizes.
findings.required_fix: Bring the ground lane window and both slot frames forward to near-flush, as the references show: outer frame face within about 0.02-0.03 m of the cladding or panel face, glass about 0.04-0.05 m behind it, with a thin reveal and the room/stair still visible behind. The corner box pane can follow the same rule. At a 0.04 m glass setback, about 0.6 m of the 0.87 m ground opening should show glass from the street camera. Rerender match_front, match_oblique, front_corner, right_side, band_contact and both phone boards, and re-review. Note: the v004 required fix asked only for widening; this setback requirement is new and comes from the v006 pixels.

source_conflict_opinions.conflict: Catalogue name/text (single-storey Garden Studio) versus three images of a two-storey house over a garage.
source_conflict_opinions.builder_resolution: Images govern; renamed Garage Suite by a person on 2026-11-19 (manifest title now 'Garage Suite').
source_conflict_opinions.reviewer_opinion: Agree. The candidate id and paths still say 'garden-studio'; keep that out of student-facing labels.

source_conflict_opinions.conflict: Ridge length: top view about 96 px (about 2 m); the oblique reference shows a longer ridge.
source_conflict_opinions.builder_resolution: 2.0 m ridge, side faces 5 in 12, front/back steeper.
source_conflict_opinions.reviewer_opinion: Agree with 2.0 m. With the builder's fitted oblique camera the eave corners register within about 10 px, but the reference ridge runs about (611,249)-(686,225), about 79 px, against the model's (606,257)-(655,230), about 56 px. In the reference the ridge is also the silhouette, with no west roof face visible, while the model shows a thin west face. Matching 79 px would need about a 3 m ridge, which would miss the top view (about 141 px against 96). The two images are not mutually consistent here. The method makes the top view the plan and ridge authority, so 2.0 m is right; the oblique residual is not a defect.

source_conflict_opinions.conflict: Stoop risers (v004 manifest said the street view shows one).
source_conflict_opinions.reviewer_opinion: Agree; both images show two risers, and the v006 manifest now says so.

reference_observations: Lock: the three reference hashes match the manifest (fdff5758..., d0913322..., e09ec32b...).

Lane face, street view: the ground window directly below the corner pane is as wide as it, with thin frames and reflective glass. Both band slots are glazed in thin frames near the band's back edge. All read near-flush at this grazing angle.
Lane face, oblique: the ground window, the lower and upper slots and the corner pane all read as glazing.
Top: perspective near-nadir view; the 96 px ridge is the plan authority.
Oblique roof: the ridge forms the silhouette and no west face is visible. This is slightly inconsistent with a 2 m ridge on the top-view outline (see source_conflict_opinions).
Porch: door and sidelight of near-equal width; two-riser stoop with the lower step in front of the post.
positive_observations: Roof fixed: a closed hip sheet with a 2.0 m ridge, seams square to each eave, hip and ridge caps with node pieces, gutter on four eaves, cedar soffit, goosenecks and downpipes to grade (top.png, roof_contact.png, reviewer r_ridge_close.png, r_eave_under_ne.png).
Massing registers to both fitted reference cameras (edge overlays: scratch crops/v6_ov_front.png, crops/v6_ov_obl.png).
Corner window now wraps visibly onto the lane face; the box is 0.05 m proud on both faces.
Two-riser stoop with the lower step in front of the post; the post bears on the 0.32 m landing; the 0.345 m threshold matches the raised hall floor. Two-step garden landing at the rear door.
Balcony: thicker cedar end with dark coping; glass guard with posts and top rail; the deck sits inside the band upstand.
Garage lites show only the garage interior; the lining gap is closed.
Lower-contrast continuous mortar; the brick no longer reads as siding, with no moire.

Openings remain full wall sections with rooms behind (glass_close.png, architecture_close.png, reviewer r_upper_room.png, r_hall_in.png). Seen square-on, the lane ground window and 0.5 m slots read well (right_side.png, band_contact.png, r_lane_low.png).
Texture-free clay: 0 images, 0 textures, 0 samplers; 17 materials; 6,624 triangles. Bounds X -0.57..8.47, Y -2.7..9.55, Z 0..7.878; nothing below grade.

No floating parts: of 680 components, the only bbox-isolated ones are cedar joint strips 6 mm proud. The new coplanar pairs are hidden contacts (stoop step faces, coping on the balcony end, base plates at grade) or lie inside the box post.
The builder's renders reproduce from this exact GLB: the reviewer rerender of rear.png differs by at most 24/255 on 724 of 1,920,000 pixels.
All whole-building views keep grade, footprint and roof in frame with neutral margin.
for_human_acceptance: Not approved: decision visual_rework_required (0 P0, 1 P1, 8 P2). A v007 should make the lane ground window and slots near-flush (V6-P1-01), fix the new lining hairline (V6-P2-01), rerender the complete set and be independently re-reviewed.
Accept or reject the inferred back and west faces (garden door with two-step landing, windows, brick wrap).
Accept the ridge resolution: 2.0 m per the top view, leaving a known residual against the oblique reference.
Runtime activation remains a separate human step under the architectural-clay profile (fixed native scale, exact variant). Runtime integration was not tested here.
limitations: AI reviewer with no builder context; not a human judgement.

The references are generated images with no scale and are not perfectly mutually consistent (see the ridge conflict). Camera fits: builder front/oblique RMS 12.4/13.9 px; reviewer top fit 12.2 px. Pixel readings are about +/- 2-3 px.
Visible-glass widths come from a reviewer ray sweep with the builder's fitted cameras on the exact GLB, with the review glass treated as the first hit. They are indicative, not photometric.

Rendered in the repository review renderer (three.js, headless SwiftShader, runtime glass replacement), not the City Prompt runtime globe. The long-range rear lines (V6-P2-04) are inferred to be a renderer artifact.
Builder evaluation files and metadata counters were not used as evidence, by instruction.
